items.name: Compaction Exponential Back-off — defer_compaction
items.counter_case: Cortex compaction is cheap (in-memory JSON rewrite); repeated attempts don't carry OS-level cost. Back-off only matters if the JSONL file is locked or disk is saturated — guard only on actual IO errors, not every call.

items.name: IDR Cyclic Slot Allocator — Entity Slot Assignment
items.symbol: struct idr { idr_rt, idr_base, idr_next }, idr_alloc(), idr_alloc_cyclic(), idr_remove(), idr_find()
items.counter_case: At <5000 entities a plain incrementing counter with a free-list Set is equivalent; the radix-tree backing of IDR only helps when IDs are sparse and the set is very large.

items.name: Three-Horizon Load Average — EXP_1/5/15 Multi-Window EWMA
items.symbol: avenrun[3], EXP_1=1884, EXP_5=2014, EXP_15=2037, calc_load(), fixed_power_int(), FSHIFT=11
items.counter_case: Three time horizons add three accumulators and three decay constants; single EWMA from pass 2 already provides a smoothed signal. Three horizons only add value when diagnosing whether pressure is a spike (diverging short vs long) or sustained.

items.name: llist MPSC Bulk-Pop — Lock-Free Event Batch Collection
items.symbol: struct llist_head { first }, struct llist_node { next }, llist_add() cmpxchg, llist_del_all() xchg, llist_reverse_order()
items.counter_case: Node.js is single-threaded; the cmpxchg/xchg atomic ops are unnecessary. The discipline of llist_del_all (swap head to null in one operation, process the detached chain) is the steal — it prevents the producer from seeing a partially-drained list.

items.name: seq_buf Fixed-Capacity Overflow-Safe Writer
items.symbol: struct seq_buf { buffer, size, len }, seq_buf_init(), seq_buf_printf(), seq_buf_has_overflowed(), seq_buf_set_overflow() sentinel len=size+1
items.counter_case: Node.js string concatenation is unbounded by default; the discipline of a fixed-size buffer only matters when the output target has a hard cap (e.g., MCP response size limit, context budget). Apply only to build_context_pack budget enforcement.

items.name: Type-Safe clamp() with Compile-Time Sign Compatibility Check
items.symbol: clamp(val, lo, hi), min_t(type, x, y), max_t(type, x, y), BUILD_BUG_ON_MSG sign check, cmp_int branchless ((l>r)-(l<r))
items.counter_case: TypeScript type system catches most signed/unsigned mixing at compile time already; clamp is a one-liner. Value is the branchless cmp_int pattern and the convention of always clamping config values rather than throwing.

items.name: eventpoll ovflist — Lost-Wakeup-Safe Event Harvest
items.symbol: struct epitem { rb_node, rdllink, ovflist next }, ovflist active during ep_send_events harvest, EP_PRIVATE_BITS
items.counter_case: Node.js EventEmitter is synchronous within a tick; events cannot arrive while the handler is running in the same tick. ovflist prevents cross-tick lost wakeups only if Cortex's event loop drains asynchronously — which it does via setTimeout/setImmediate.

items.name: log2.h roundup_pow_of_two — Ring-Buffer Size Convention
items.counter_case: TypeScript/JS has no compile-time constant folding for these; is_power_of_2 is a one-liner (n & (n-1)) === 0. The steal is adding it as a shared util and a CLAUDE.md rule that all ring-buffer capacities must be power-of-2.

items.name: WQ_FLAG_EXCLUSIVE Thundering-Herd Prevention
items.counter_case: The IngestCompletion from pass 4 already resolves all waiters simultaneously; exclusive wakeup is only needed if Cortex wants to throttle how many waiters proceed at once — not currently needed.

items.name: DEFINE_HASHTABLE O(1) Entity Lookup by Key
items.symbol: DEFINE_HASHTABLE(name, bits), hash_add(), hash_del(), hash_for_each_possible(), HASH_SIZE
items.counter_case: JavaScript Map already provides O(1) amortized lookup with no manual bucket management; DEFINE_HASHTABLE is valuable as a fixed-size alternative that avoids Map's dynamic resizing — only relevant if entity count is fixed and GC pressure from Map rehashing is measurable.

items.name: plist Priority-Sorted Work Queue — O(K) Insert by Priority Level
items.symbol: struct plist_node { prio, prio_list, node_list }, plist_add(), plist_del(), plist_first(), INT_MIN=highest priority
items.counter_case: With only 3 priority levels (HIGH/NORMAL/LOW) three separate queues with an if-chain is O(1) and simpler than plist. plist shines with many priority levels (RT has 99); Cortex has 3.

items.name: glob_match __pure Memoizable Glob Filter
items.counter_case: Cortex already uses micromatch for glob; the __pure annotation is the steal — it signals that the result can be memoized. Add a Map<pat+str, bool> result cache keyed on the pair to avoid re-evaluating the same pattern against the same path.

items.name: folio_mark_accessed referenced-Bit 2nd-Access Promotion
items.symbol: folio_mark_accessed(), referenced bit, folio_activate(), cpu_fbatches.lru_activate per-CPU deferred promotion
items.counter_case: The Two-Tier CLOCK from pass 2 already implements the 2nd-access promotion; folio_mark_accessed adds the referenced-bit intermediate step to distinguish 'accessed once' from 'about to be promoted'. Refinement of existing pattern, not a new one.

items.name: sort_r Closure Comparator + cmp_int Branchless Three-Way
items.symbol: sort_r(base, num, size, cmp_func, swap_func, priv), cmp_int = ((l > r) - (l < r))
items.counter_case: Array.prototype.sort() with a closure already provides the priv-context pattern natively in JS; branchless comparator is a micro-optimization irrelevant at Cortex's sort sizes.

items.name: Signed/Unsigned Comparison Without Explicit Cast
items.symbol: BUILD_BUG_ON_MSG type-compatibility check in min()/max() — mixing signed/unsigned is a compile error
items.pattern: Cortex's scoring and threshold comparisons mix signed scores (can be negative on error) with unsigned sizes (buffer lengths, entity counts) in the same comparison without explicit casts. TypeScript allows this silently; the Linux minmax.h approach makes it a compile error.
items.proposed_action: Add ESLint rule @typescript-eslint/no-unsafe-comparison or a custom rule flagging comparisons between `number` fields from score-bearing types (which can be negative) and size/count fields (which should be non-negative). Add a CLAUDE.md rule: score fields are always `number` (can be negative), size/count fields are always `number & { __brand: 'NonNegative' }` — use branded types to make sign mismatch a TS error.

items.name: rb_root_cached O(1) Minimum Tracking
items.violated_principle: At <5000 entities the IntrusiveLRU tail pointer (pass 4) already provides O(1) minimum/maximum; an augmented red-black tree adds O(log n) insert cost for a use case where O(n) array scan is already <1ms — domain mismatch at scale
